newsitem.title: UAE: Iran police detain protesters at German embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran police detain protesters at German embassy.

text.p: Iranian riot police on Monday arrested Islamist students protesting at the German embassy in Tehran who said they would seize the mission unless Bonn apologised for a court verdict accusing Iran of ordering political killings, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.
Witnesses said several hundred demonstrators charged lines of riot police guarding the embassy in an apparent effort to occupy the compound but were pushed back.
"The special guards protecting the German embassy in Tehran arrested some of the university students who attempted to break into the security line of the embassy," IRNA said.

"A spokesman of the students warned the embassy officials that they would seize the embassy unless the German government make a formal apology to the Iranian nation and retreat from hostility against Iran."

Police, standing six rows deep around the barricaded embassy in central Tehran, used sticks to stop several charges by the students who chanted "Death to Germany" and the Moslem rallying cry "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest).

Leaders of the protest appealed for calm through loudspeakers to hold back the demonstrators, some of whom threw stones, the witnesses said. The angry students dispersed after the clashes which lasted less than half an hour.

It was the third demonstration held at the embassy since Friday, a day after a Berlin court sentenced to jail three Lebanese men and an Iranian for the 1992 killing of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant. The court said senior Iranian leaders had ordered the killings.

"By taking their recent move, the Germans were caught in a trap set by the Zionists, thus harming the century-old relations between Tehran and Bonn," Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Monday in remarks reported by IRNA.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.
Chanting crowds marched in towns and cities across Iran on Monday to protest at the ruling, state-run Tehran radio said.
IRNA said a large number of veterans disabled by Iraqi chemical attacks in the 1980-88 war between the two neighbours would march on Wednesday to the embassy.
The war veterans would also protest against German firms which provided toxic chemicals to Iraq, it said.
Iran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during its war with Iran.
Iran has responded to the withdrawal of all European Union ambassadors except Greece's by announcing it will pull its envoys out of those countries in return.
Rafsanjani said on Friday that the diplomatic row was a "passing storm".
Germany made clear at the weekend it would seek to avoid stepping up the dispute with Iran over the ruling.

Bonn officials say privately that, behind the scenes, Iran has signalled it does not wish to raise the temperature in the diplomatic stand-off with a country which, until recently, was its biggest trade partner and friend in the West.
